summary: Amos 3 (15 verses) continues the story of justice. Starting with 'Hear this word that Yahweh has spoken against you, children of Israel, against the whole family which I brought up out of the land of Egypt, saying:', it moves through themes of justice, righteousness and calls readers toward righteousness.
whyItMatters: This chapter matters because it shows justice lived out in prosperous but unjust. For a first-time reader, it answers: who is God in this moment, what does he ask, and how do people respond.

keyVerses.text: Hear this word that Yahweh has spoken against you, children of Israel, against the whole family which I brought up out of the land of Egypt, saying:
The lion has roared. Who will not fear? The Lord Yahweh has spoken. Who can but prophesy?
I will strike the winter house with the summer house; and the houses of ivory will perish, and the great houses will have an end,” says Yahweh.

questions.question: What is happening in Amos 3?
questions.answer: In 15 verses, this chapter amos 3 (15 verses) continues the story of justice. starting with 'hear this word that yahweh has spoken against you, children of israel, against the whole family which i brought up out of the land of egypt, saying:', it moves through themes of justice, righteousness and calls readers toward righteousness. The setting is prosperous but unjust, written to northern israel. Look for who speaks, who listens, and what changes by the end.

questions.question: Who wrote Amos and why 3 matters in the bigger story?
questions.answer: Traditionally amos, shepherd, addressed to northern israel around ~760 bc. This chapter fits the book's purpose as oracles — its themes of justice, righteousness build on what came before.

questions.question: What does 'prophet' mean in this chapter?
questions.answer: Messenger speaking for God. In this chapter, it appears in context of justice. For a first-time reader: think of it as messenger speaking for god, not just religious jargon.

questions.question: What does this chapter teach about God or people?
questions.answer: Through justice and righteousness, it shows God's character (faithful, just, merciful) and human tendency (need, failure, hope). Notice how verses move from problem to provision.

questions.question: Verse 12 is long — what is it saying in plain English?
questions.answer: The verse says: 'Yahweh says: “As the shepherd rescues out of the mouth of the lion two legs, or a piece of an ear, so shall the children of Israel be rescued who sit in Samaria on the corner of a ...' In plain terms: it is making a key point about justice. Break it into two halves — what is described, and what is promised or commanded.

questions.question: How could this chapter apply today without forcing modern ideas onto it?
questions.answer: Ask: what was original audience supposed to do with this? Then ask: what similar situation exists today? For example, if chapter warns about idols, today that might be money or status; if it celebrates deliverance, where do people need deliverance today?
